name: Thermistor motor protection relay
summary: Relay that monitors PTC thermistors embedded in motor windings and trips when their resistance rises at the rated temperature.
description: A thermistor protection relay is connected to a chain of PTC thermistors built into a motor's windings. When the windings reach the thermistors' rated response temperature, their resistance rises sharply and the relay opens its contact in the motor control circuit, protecting against overheating that a current-based overload cannot detect.

Typical causes it catches are blocked ventilation, high ambient temperature and frequent starting. The symbol does not show whether the relay detects a short-circuited sensor loop, whether it latches, or how it is reset, which affect safety where automatic restart is possible.
readingNotes: Follow the sensor loop to the motor terminal box.
Check reset type and short-circuit detection.
distinction: A thermistor relay measures winding temperature directly; a thermal overload relay models heating from current.
